A SHA-256 digest can contain a Luhn-valid 13-to-19 digit run by coincidence, and test-kits/integrity-manifest.json is a file of 83 such digests rewritten whenever any protected file changes. This branch was first spelled `WP-0A-CON-008-sweep-age-floor`; the resulting digest of work-packages/WP-0A-CON-008.json contained a Visa-shaped 13-digit run that scan-repository-secrets.mjs correctly reported as a payment card number. It was a false positive with no data behind it, and there is no allowlist to silence one -- deliberately, per that scanner's own comments. The branch was renamed to `WP-0A-CON-008-pid-reuse-age-floor` to change the digest, which is a workaround and not a fix: roughly one regenerated digest in a few hundred will trip this again, on any package, for reasons having nothing to do with that package's work. The scanner is outside this package's writable paths and an exemption there is explicitly reserved for a reviewed decision with a named owner. The offending run is not reproduced here, because that rule is not prose-exempt and quoting it fails the scan -- which this entry established by doing it. Recorded so the next author finds a diagnosis, not a mystery.
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. Reverting restores a comparison point that is main whenever a branch has merged main into itself, which leaves check:handoff red with 'on no path to this branch' and refresh:handoff refusing to rewrite it -- so a reverted branch must be kept linear, as batch 040's was.
